_comment: System lines: tutorial, PIP hints, dawn notes, Earth messages, storm results, reveal. Keys are referenced by events.json and by the engines. Tokens in braces are filled at runtime (see events.json _comment, plus {peakRate} {peakTime} {peakRatio} {cmeSpeed} {cmeTime} {date} {kp} {window}). Reading level: grade 3-5. Portions generated with the assistance of an SI tool (Claude) and reviewed by Team PlutonyX.

intro.say: Mars. Jezero Crater. Three and a half billion years ago, this was a lake.
Four people live on its shore now. In ten sols, their ship goes home.

tutorial.say: Good morning, Commander. Sol 1 of 10. A sol is one day on Mars. It is a little longer than a day on Earth.
The night was cold and the battery is tired. Today's sunlight gives us a few power cells. Four machines want them.
Air Maker, Greenhouse, Storm Shield, Rover. We can't feed them all. Tap the plus and minus buttons to share out the power.
Watch the arrows. Each one shows what will go up and what will go down tonight.
There is no perfect answer. There is only what you choose to protect.
When you are ready, press Confirm. I will show you what happened in the morning.

hints.alloc.lowAir: PIP: air is low. Give the Air Maker at least Normal today.
hints.alloc.lowPower: PIP: the battery is nearly empty. Turn something down or tonight will be cold.
hints.alloc.plantsWilting: PIP: the plants are wilting. One more dark sol could end the garden.
hints.alloc.stormWatch: PIP: a storm may be coming. Shield charge takes several sols to build.
hints.alloc.balanced: PIP's plan: keep the air steady first, then split what is left.
hints.alloc.overspend: Not enough power for that. Turn something else down first.
hints.storm.needShield: PIP: the shield needs {need} percent for this storm. It has {shield}.
hints.general.askEarth: PIP: Earth is {delayMin} light-minutes away. Any answer arrives after you have to choose.

dawn.clear: Clear sky. The panels are drinking sunlight.
dawn.haze: Hazy sky. The panels get a little less sunlight today.
dawn.dust: Dust storm. The sky is brown and the panels are starving.
dawn.deepDust: The dust is thick as night. Almost no sunlight reaches the panels.
dawn.dustEnds: The dust is settling. You can see the crater rim again.
dawn.panelsDusty: A layer of dust is still on the panels. They make a little less power.
dawn.flare1: The Sun is active today: a class {flareMax} flare in NASA's record.
dawn.flare2: Strong solar flare today: class {flareMax}. X is the strongest kind.
dawn.flare3: Huge solar flare today: class {flareMax}. One of the biggest of this solar cycle.
dawn.radio1: Solar static on the radio. Messages from Earth may be noisy.
dawn.radio2: Earth is having its own storm today. Mission Control is hard to reach.
dawn.earthAurora: Tonight people on Earth are seeing auroras. The same Sun is busy for both planets. Earth's storm index hit {kp} out of 9.
dawn.cloudArrives: The solar cloud that NASA's model predicted has reached Mars. On the ground, the radiation counter reads {doseToday} micrograys for the day. A calm day is about {calmDose}.
dawn.cloudDip: Odd. Since the solar clouds started passing, the radiation counter has gone down a little. Scientists have a name for that dip. Open the Science Log to learn why.
dawn.stormContinues: The storm is not over. Radiation is still {ratio} times a calm day. Shield charge still matters tonight.
dawn.stormOver: The radiation counter is back to normal. The storm has passed.
dawn.dilAway: Dil is in the field. Her bunk is empty and her tea mug is on the console.
dawn.dilHome: The rover rolled into the garage before dawn. Dil is home, and the core is in the cold box.
dawn.plantsLow: The plants are drooping. Ana is quiet this morning.
dawn.plantsDead: The greenhouse is dark. Nothing in it is alive.
dawn.sunspot: PIP: my Sun camera shows a very large group of sunspots coming around the edge of the Sun. From here I can see it. Earth cannot.

because.lowAirTired: Because the air was thin for two sols, the crew is tired and slow.
because.coldNight: Because the battery ran flat, the heaters shut off in the night. Frost on the inside of the windows.
because.noHarvestHungry: Because the garden never gave a harvest, the food shelves are getting empty.
because.gardenDark: Because the greenhouse went dark, the plants lost leaves.
because.gardenDied: Because the greenhouse stayed dark too long, the garden died.
because.shieldHeld: Because the shield was charged, the storm stayed outside.
because.shieldThin: Because the shield was only partly charged, some of the storm got through.
because.shieldEmpty: Because the shield was almost empty, the storm came straight through the walls.
because.waterWallHelped: Because the walls were full of water, less radiation reached the crew.
because.waterLowAfterWall: Because the water went into the walls, the taps are running slow.
because.roverCharged: Because the rover was well charged, Dil made it home.
because.roverFlat: Because the rover was low on charge, Dil was stuck at the cliff. Getting her back cost power and sleep.

earth.forecast.say: Lakeshore, Mission Control. About that forecast. A solar cloud reaching Mars often changes very little on the ground. The thing to fear is a very fast eruption: its particles can arrive in under an hour.
If you see one start, do not wait for us. We are with you.

earth.spots.say: Lakeshore, we have your photos. Nobody here is sitting down. If you can bring that core home safely, bring it. If you can't, bring yourselves.

earth.storm.say: Lakeshore, we just got your storm call. By now it is over for you, one way or another. We could not see that side of the Sun from here. You could.
Whatever you chose, you chose it with better eyes than ours. We are with you.

earth.generic.say: Lakeshore, Mission Control. We got your question. By the time you hear this, you have already decided. Tell us how it went. We are with you.

storm.peak: Radiation peak: {peakRate} micrograys per hour at {peakTime} UTC. A calm hour is about {calmRate}.

result.held.say: Shield held. Every badge is green. I'd like to never do that again.

result.thin.say: Some of it got through. Nobody is hurt. But the badges are fuller than I like, and I am watching all of you.

result.failed.say: The shield ran dry halfway. Nobody is sick. But the rules are clear about what these badges mean.

dil.recalled.lost.say: I'm in. I'm fine. The core is still in the rock, and I can't go back for it. Don't talk to me yet.

dil.recalled.kept.say: I'm in. And look what was already sealed in the cold box. I drilled faster than I thought.

dil.cliff.ok.say: Sat under forty metres of rock with a core in my lap. Best seat on Mars. Coming home at first light.

dil.cliff.stranded.say: Good news: I have the core. Bad news: the rover won't start. I'm going to need a tow.

dil.trust.shelter.say: You said my call. I stayed. I had rock above me and the core in my hands. Thank you for trusting me.

dil.trust.run.say: You said my call. I looked at the sky and I ran. The core stayed. I think I'd run again.

dil.grounded.say: Dil, your badge is over the mission limit. You're not sick. But you're done with outside work. Doctor's orders, and the rulebook's.

dil.sentHome.say: Dil's badge is in the red. She feels fine. She rides home in the medical bay, and Earth checks her over. No arguments.

fragments._comment: Every answer from Earth carries one more piece of the broken Sol 1 message (max 3). Other events can add pieces too.
fragments.intro: PIP: while the dish was listening, I caught another piece of the broken message.
pieces: "...the sunspot group that lit our skies has turned out of our sight and into yours..."
"...we cannot see what it does next..."
"...you are our eyes now. Do not wait for us."
fragments.complete: PIP: that is all of it. The message is whole.

reveal.title: It really happened.
reveal.lead: Every solar storm in this mission was real. One sol in the game was one real day.
reveal.footer: Space weather: NASA DONKI. Radiation on Mars: NASA's Curiosity rover (RAD), from NASA's RadLab. Dust, breakdowns and the crew are our story.
reveal.live: This mission ran on live NASA space weather from {window}.
reveal.injected: The Sun was calm in those days, so the storm on Sol 8 replayed the real storm of 20 May 2024 from NASA's archive.

debrief.title: Mission debrief
debrief.tryAgain: Fly again. The Sun stays the same, but dust and breakdowns will be different.
debrief.partial: Not everything made it. Look at what did.

discussion.q: Which machine did your team turn down first? What did it cost you later?
The forecast said a solar cloud was coming. Did you charge the shield? What did you give up to do it?
Earth could not help during the storm. Why not? How long did a message take to arrive?
If you were Dil, would you have stayed with the core or driven home? Is there a right answer?
